rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 6 'What happened' line 52: 'The loop that started with a failing test closed.' 'The loop' has no antecedent earlier IN THIS FILE, but resolves via module include-order (rule 1's own clause): host module curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md names it twice before this exercise's include -- '## What You'll Learn' bullet 1 ('Run an orient -> fix -> close -> compound loop end-to-end...', line 16) and '## Key Concepts' ('The loop is orient -> fix -> close -> compound', line 46) -- both precede the '## Start here' list (line 33) that includes close-the-ticket.md third of four. The noun phrase is also self-defining via its own relative clause ('that started with a failing test'). Stays inside. Chunk 0's 'the bug you fixed'/'the bug's ticket' (lines 5,7,13) and chunk 6's 'a failing test' (line 52) resolve under the session-artifact carve-out. Chunk 4's 'it' (line 43, 'Does it sound like...') is immediate continuation of chunk 3's close-out subject (lines 33-39). No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

Only external pointer: chunk 3 line 35, '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)' -- named by title, not located by position (satisfies the navigational-pointer carve-out). Verified via `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --links curriculum/exercises/close-the-ticket.md`, which lists exactly this one link for the file with the document title as anchor text. No 'the opening lecture said' style backward callback to another file by position anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Shortest chunk is 4 ('Double-check the voice', lines 41-44): its one bullet ('Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket? If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it.') carries a self-sufficient compare-and-correct instruction, not a bare wait-state. No chunk in the six-chunk deck is context-dependent-only.

Checked all six headers against their chunk content: 'Read the ticket for your bug' -> opens+pastes ticket link (11-19); 'Read the conventions off the ticket' -> field-convention read + five-rule ask (20-32); 'Write the close-out and send it' -> drafts+posts close-out (33-40); 'Double-check the voice' -> register check (41-44); 'Anything can be reverse-engineered' -> generalises the move, declarative per rule 15's named exception (45-49); 'What happened' -> recap (50-55). Closest-to-violating: chunk 5's declarative header against line 47's supporting claim -- header and content agree, no contradiction.

Scanned all seven chunks against all six sub-patterns. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.': the file's only two 'not' occurrences (line 23 'not the policy', line 47 'you did not write') are single negations, no repeated triple -- verified via `awk 'NR>=1 && NR<=55' curriculum/exercises/close-the-ticket.md | grep -niE '\bnot\b'` (2 hits, neither part of a triple). Anaphora/epistrophe triples: none. Self-grading superlative (the blocking sub-item): closest line is chunk 3 line 35, '...and it pays back on every session after this one' -- a factual/mechanical persistence claim about an installed connector, not graded language ('one of the most/best'); stays inside. Number+retraction: none (only plain counts: '20 minutes', 'five bug rules', neither hedged). Abstraction-noun stacks: none -- vocabulary stays concrete (ticket, tracker, connector, close-out). Empty-leg verb triplets: none.
